notes: PO-increase items record the increase, not the new cumulative total; consistent across the sample, but the site should label it as an increase. 2025-06-24: every consent item in actions.json (21 items) is labeled section 12; the minutes number the consent agenda as section 10, so all 21 refs at that meeting look systematically off by section number (resolution numbers are unaffected). Same section-number error at 2025-09-23 (24 consent items labeled 12x, minutes say 10x) and 2025-10-14 (59 items labeled 12x, minutes say 10x). Meetings 2025-05-13, 2025-05-27 and 2025-11-18 really do number the consent agenda 12 (they have extra appointment/election sections), which is probably where the extractor picked up the habit. hialeah-2025-12-09-10L should not be shown as having a no vote; display as 5-0 or as unclear, not 5-1. Method: every sampled item was checked against the minutes PDF through WebFetch with prompts asking for verbatim quotes of the item caption, resolution/ordinance number, parties, amounts and the printed vote line (plus AYE/NAY blocks where present); section headings were pulled separately to check item numbering. This is the same fetch tool the list was built with, so it is not a fully independent read of the PDF; but quotes were requested verbatim and it did push back when an item did not exist (06/24/2025 '12D'). Where the minutes themselves are internally inconsistent (tally vs AYE block, owner-name typos) the list generally took the printed result line or the more plausible spelling; those are logged as severity 'info' and not counted as errors. All 65 dissent/denied actions matched the minutes on mover-independent fields (who voted no/absent, tally, result).

sampleDesign.randomStratified: one per meeting date (36 dates) + 24 more at random from non-dissent items

errorRates.ref: 6/125 (4.8%); 6/60 (10%) of the random stratum; 0/65 of dissent/denied
